fit.gap_handling_summary: The strongest genuine matches—Kafka incident handling, regular on-call, English-language work and knowledge-sharing—are prominent. Python, Go, AWS and Terraform limitations are accurately qualified. However, professional backend tenure, database work, REST delivery, testing and deployment ownership cannot be established from the supplied notes; the documents should not be read as demonstrating those requirements. Missing information needs clarification rather than invention.

issues: No candidate name, email, telephone number or other usable contact information appears.
The sole employment entry has neither a job title nor employment dates, so professional seniority and duration cannot be assessed.
Reverse chronology is trivially satisfied by a single employer, but the missing employment dates prevent meaningful chronology checking.
The placeholders are honest about unavailable information but make the CV look unfinished and unsuitable for submission.
The summary is weighted toward operational support rather than evidence of building backend services; the source material does not establish the latter.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in a sensible order with intact words and recognizable section headings.
No employment dates or job title establish the required three years of professional backend development.
Many central requirements, particularly databases, REST APIs, Docker and automated testing, are absent and not established by the source material.
Python is present but explicitly limited to scripting; Java certification is not proof of professional Java backend tenure.
EKS supplies a recognizable Kubernetes-related term, but the literal Kubernetes keyword is absent.
Placeholder identity and contact fields may impair candidate-record extraction.

issues: Two consecutive sentences repeat AWS exposure to EKS, S3 and SQS almost verbatim.
The final paragraph repeats the opening list of incident response, documentation, on-call and knowledge-sharing rather than adding evidence.
The letter ends with 'Kind regards,' but no candidate name or signature.
Company specificity is limited to the named team, shipment-event reliability and on-call work; it does not develop a distinctive motivation for Tessel.
It provides little evidence of backend implementation because none was supplied; an application-ready version needs clarification of actual engineering work.
strengths: Correct company, role and team throughout.
Connects a concrete Kafka incident and regular on-call work to relevant team responsibilities.
Clearly distinguishes Python scripting from production service development and Go learning from professional work.
Accurately limits AWS and Terraform experience.
Professional English and a reasonable one-page length.

culture_used: Reliability and ownership of production services

spacing_issues: The cover letter leaves substantial lower-page whitespace, consistent with the measured 51.7% fill; this is acceptable for a short letter but the unsigned closing makes it look incomplete.
issues: The CV's largest visual element is '[Not provided]', drawing immediate attention to missing identity information.
Missing title, dates and repository URL are visibly embedded in otherwise polished CV sections.
The cover letter has no name beneath its closing.
Both images otherwise show clean serif typography, aligned text, clear hierarchy and adequate margins; the measurements report no overflow.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'bring production-support experience and operational exposure to AWS services including EKS, S3, and SQS. I also have user-level operational exposure to EKS, S3, and SQS' is conspicuously repetitive; combine it into one sentence.
'I am also developing Go through a personal OpenAPI specification-diff CLI project' is awkward: 'developing my Go skills through...' would be clearer.

'my Kafka event-streaming, production incident investigation, post-incident documentation, on-call support, and backend knowledge-sharing experience' is a heavy closing list that largely repeats the introduction.
'Go is a learning project' is imprecise shorthand; the candidate is learning Go through a project, rather than Go itself being the project.

evaluation.summary: The documents are unusually careful about evidence: they preserve the distinction between scripting, learning projects and professional operational experience without inventing backend tenure or production Python work. Kafka incident response, on-call responsibility and English-language work are relevant strengths, but the required backend-development duration and several core technical requirements remain unestablished. The CV is not submission-ready because its identity, contact details, job title and employment dates are placeholders, while the letter is unsigned and repeats AWS experience almost verbatim. Both PDFs are readable and cleanly structured, but the missing information and weak evidence for core requirements make screening success unlikely.
